title: Small trial finds ear device for high BP safe and easy to use at home

author: AADRITA HALDER
title: 'Can't use it to kill people': Musk admits restricting Starlink in Ukraine

author: TOI
description: Returning professionals are just one part of a wider flow of talent. Indians are coming back after years abroad. Members of the diaspora are sharing specialist knowledge from where they are. International experts are arriving for a defined period to build skills and pass them on. The pull is increasingly professional. India now hosts 2,117 global capability centres employing 2.36 million people, according to the Nasscom-Zinnov GCC Landscape 2026.
title: India wants to become a global talent hub. What needs to change?

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: NASA administrator Jared Isaacman provided an update regarding the Artemis III lunar mission and upcoming docking exercises. The agency plans for significant interactions with Elon Musk's SpaceX and Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin next year. Docking practices will involve astronaut teams launching aboard NASA's Orion capsule from Cape Canaveral. Isaacman indicated that the competition has intensified due to historical precedents set by earlier space missions.
title: Nasa’s Isaacman shares Artemis IV update as SpaceX, Blue Origin plan Moon base

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has issued a stark warning about the looming Iranian nuclear threat. Analyst Yuval Blumberg emphasizes the urgency of the next two years for Israel to take decisive measures. He cautioned against letting internal political matters overshadow critical national security issues, especially with the parliamentary election approaching on October 27. Trump's support of Netanyahu further solidifies their alliance as essential in addressing Iran's ambitions.
title: ‘Nuclear threat will overshadow all’: Netanyahu’s Iran warning ahead of polls

author: SRINATH VUDALI
description: Archana Chowdhury Malik, a 29-year-old software employee, was discovered dead by hanging in Hyderabad. The incident occurred in an apartment located in Chandra Nayak Thanda. Police received information about her death and quickly arrived at the scene. Authorities have registered a case and are investigating the circumstances of her passing.
title: Hyd techie found dead after threatening to take her life during video call to boyfriend

author: VIVEK DUBEY
title: DK Shivakumar's big warning to B'luru IT firms over sidelining Kannadiga candidates

author: AASTHA JHA
description: On November 1, Rahul Gandhi is set to lead a rally to rally citizens against alleged vote theft, spotlighting issues like voter list inaccuracies and the response to complainants. The BJP has voiced concerns over the timing due to its proximity to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots memorial. Several organizations, including Delhi's Chamber of Trade and Industry, have expressed disapproval.
title: 'Thanks BJP for promoting': Rahul takes swipe at govt over Nov 1 rally in Delhi

author: PRIYANKA JAISWAL
title: 'Not less than a pilgrimage’: PM Modi marks 12 years of Mann Ki Baat - top quotes

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: India A struggled initially but found stability through an unbeaten partnership between Devdutt Padikkal and Sai Sudharsan. Padikkal scored 56 runs, while Sudharsan contributed 39 runs, helping the team recover. After a poor start, the duo added 96 runs without losing another wicket by the end of Day 2. Earlier, India's bowlers did well as Anshul Kamboj and Auqib Nabi took three wickets each.
title: Devdutt Padikkal, Sai Sudharsan hit back after KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal failures

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: Protests in Tirana escalated into clashes as demonstrators faced off with riot police during an anti-government rally. Protesters expressed their anger over alleged government corruption, unemployment, and education issues. The demonstrations also targeted government buildings and banks, leading to significant unrest in the city. The student-led protests represented a wider movement against corruption and called for governmental reforms.
title: Watch: Protesters launch fireworks at police as fiery clashes take place in Albania

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: As Dalal Street braces for a pivotal week, key earnings reports and the impending US Federal Reserve interest rate decision are grabbing attention. Investors are eagerly anticipating the September industrial production and manufacturing figures, set to be released on October 28. Moreover, Jio Platforms' stock market entry promises to sway investor sentiment.
title: Stock market outlook: Fed meeting, crude & more - top cues guiding Dalal Street this week

author: SHARIQ MAJEED
description: A 28-year-old woman has taken the brave step of reporting her husband after an alleged assault sparked by a dispute over a vehicle. CCTV footage depicts the disturbing encounter, while neighbors came to her aid upon hearing her screams. Police are currently eyeing the medico-legal report as they prepare to move forward with the case.
title: ‘Buy me Thar’: Woman slapped, kicked, dragged by hair by husband over vehicle demand

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: Donald Trump asserted at a rally that the United States has secured Greenland and Venezuela as territories. His statements were made despite the lack of legal transfer of sovereignty over Greenland from Denmark. A recent memorandum of understanding focused on maritime cooperation, which does not include Greenland. Trump also announced a significant investment by Audi in Georgia, emphasizing job creation.
title: Trump claims US has secured Greenland, Venezuela in ‘greatest real estate deal’

author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
description: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.
title: From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at Asian Para Games

author: AASTHA JHA
description: In his latest statements, external affairs minister S Jaishankar called for a more robust leadership from the UN to confront pressing world issues. He highlighted a significant gap in global decision-making that leaves many regions, particularly in the Global South, behind in critical areas like finance, fuel, food, and fertilizer. Emphasizing the importance of fair AI development, Jaishankar encourages strategies that ensure widespread access to its benefits, fostering international cooperation.
title: 'Don't be spectator, show leadership': EAM Jaishankar to UN on terrorism, global crises

author: SOUMITRA BOSE
description: After a complaint from a concerned landlord, the Wathoda police raided a rented apartment, revealing a trove of counterfeit Rs 500 notes, printing machinery, and a laptop. Preliminary findings suggest that this operation may be connected to an extensive counterfeit currency syndicate. The principal suspect, Pushpam Bhandane, remains at large, prompting a coordinated search effort involving the anti-terrorism squad and other investigative bodies.
title: ‘Failed to pay rent’: How landlord’s complaint led to 1,600 fake Rs 500 notes

author: P NAVEEN
description: Prabhulal Gupta, a 65-year-old man, tragically died in Ganjbasoda after an apparent accident involving an overhead power line. Residents reported that his spit, while chewing gutkha, made contact with the 11kV line. Locals expressed anger towards the electricity company for neglecting their complaints about unsafe wiring. His landlord mentioned that officials had assured residents about addressing these high-tension line concerns.
title: Man spits gutkha from 3rd-floor balcony, dies after coming in contact with 11kV wire

author: ABHISHEK MISHRA
description: The Centre has deployed two Rapid Action Force companies comprising around 250 CRPF personnel to Arunachal Pradesh following violent protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project. A mob torched an NHPC office and a police station in Pasighat, injuring over 40 police personnel. The project, seen as a strategic counter to China’s mega dam, faces opposition from indigenous tribes fearing displacement and submergence of villages.
title: Centre rushes 250 RAF personnel to Arunachal after protests over hydropower project

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: Between October 26 and October 29, five companies will debut their initial public offerings, aiming to raise an impressive Rs 2,600 crore from the primary market. These firms—EAAA India Alternatives, SFC Environmental Technologies, M K Sons Fine Jewels, BLS Polymers, and Bombay Coated and Special Steels—will utilize the capital for business expansion, working capital augmentation, and settling debts. More companies are gearing up for IPO launches set for November 5.
title: Five IPOs to hit Dalal Street next week, targeting nearly Rs 2,600 cr from investors

author: PRANJAL PANDEY
description: Iran's armed forces conducted a drone attack on the Komala group in Iraq's Kurdistan region. This operation reportedly caused significant damage and casualties to the group's infrastructure. Previous strikes on the Komala group have occurred since the regional conflict began in February. Iran accuses these opposition groups of receiving support from Israel, its longstanding adversary. The Kurdish opposition has denied allegations of receiving arms from Israel despite Iran's claims.
title: Drone attack: Iran targets Kurdish opposition bases in Iraq

author: TRISHA TEWARI
description: The growing preference for short-form digital content is raising concerns about children’s ability to engage with books and sustain attention. Educationists and experts examine declining reading habits, the role of examination-driven learning, and the impact of digital distractions. Drawing on research and Kerala’s library movement, the story explores ways to rebuild deep reading through schools, families and communities.
title: From unfinished books to 10-second reels: Is reading becoming lost art?

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged citizens to support local artisans by prioritizing their products while shopping for festivals. He emphasized that doing so would strengthen the 'Vocal for Local' campaign and promote a self-reliant India. Modi highlighted successful local exports such as makhana and arhar dal to various international markets. Additionally, he discussed efforts aimed at reviving traditional skills and farming practices, including natural cotton cultivation.
title: ‘Give priority to local artisans’: PM Modi’s festive shopping appeal as Diwali approaches

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: Babar Azam's recent performances in the ODI tri-series have raised concerns regarding his ability to convert starts into significant scores. He scored 45 against Sri Lanka and 34 against England, failing to build on important beginnings. Former cricketer Tanveer Ahmed has highlighted weaknesses in Babar's batting against spinners, incoming fast deliveries, and short balls. He emphasized the need for Babar to address these vulnerabilities to improve his performance.
title: 'When will you score runs?' Babar Azam's weaknesses exposed by ex-Pakistan player

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: Foreign Portfolio Investors have withdrawn Rs 48,056 crore from Indian equities during October due to high crude oil prices. Selling eased slightly in a recent week, with some FPIs becoming net buyers for two days. Elevated oil prices and inflation concerns are contributing to deteriorating corporate earnings outlooks affecting investor confidence. Domestic institutional investors have somewhat mitigated the selling pressure on markets in recent weeks.
title: Foreign investors withdraw Rs 48,056 crore in October as market selling continues

author: ABHISHEK MISHRA
title: ‘JD(U) is finished’: Bihar strongman Anant Singh to float own party after expulsion

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Tehran's policies will not change regardless of potential war. He warned that resuming conflict would alter the security landscape in the Strait of Hormuz significantly. Following recent comments from US President Donald Trump, fears of renewed military action against Iran are escalating. Araghchi emphasized the need for rationality to avoid another military confrontation.
title: 'War or no war, our policies remain unchanged': Iran FM Araghchi amid fresh US strike fears

author: AASTHA JHA
title: Who is Gadi Eisenkot? Ex-army chief of Israel is Netanyahu's biggest challenger

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: Bangladesh has requested detailed information from Saudi Arabia about the execution of two citizens. The two individuals were executed for committing an indecent act inside a mosque in Makkah. A diplomatic letter was sent seeking clarification on their legal representation during trials and other circumstances. Dhaka is also looking for explanations regarding discrepancies in the charges against these citizens.
title: Were they beheaded? Bangladesh seeks answers from Saudi over execution of 'couple'

author: HADI KHAN
description: Posters demanding 200 Assembly seats have surfaced outside the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee headquarters in Lucknow. Congress aims to strengthen its position ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections by negotiating a larger seat share. The party has reportedly submitted a wishlist to its ally, Samajwadi Party, complicating seat-sharing discussions. State Congress leaders are using a grading model to evaluate constituencies based on organisational growth.
title: ‘200 seats haq hai hamara’: Congress puts its UP poll ambitions on Lucknow walls

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: HDFC Bank and Bajaj Finance experienced significant market value declines last week amid broader market losses. The combined drop in valuations for eight major companies totaled Rs 1.55 lakh crore. Market capitalization for BSE-listed companies fell sharply by Rs 20,78,774.28 crore. Only Tata Consultancy Services and Larsen & Toubro managed to increase their market valuations during this period.
title: Market recap: Eight of top 10 firms lose Rs 1.55 lakh crore

author: MAHIMA SHARMA
description: A drone strike carried out by Ukrainian forces hit Belgorod, leading to two confirmed deaths and injuring at least 13 people. Local officials highlighted significant destruction to housing, vehicles, and local infrastructure. Additionally, a nearby village reported another fatality and injuries stemming from the ongoing hostilities. These events underscore the ongoing violence escalating along the Russia-Ukraine border, and tensions continue to mount in the region.
title: Ukraine drone attacks kill three, injure 14 in Russia’s Belgorod region

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: Thousands of people protested across Europe over the weekend, demanding action against rising living costs and government corruption. Demonstrations were reported in France, Italy, Albania, Spain, and Portugal, with varying degrees of violence. Clashes between protesters and police resulted in numerous arrests and injuries in several countries. Many demonstrators called for affordable housing, better education, and protection of public pensions.
title: Protests engulf Europe: People take to streets in France, Albania, Italy, Spain, Portugal

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Nilesh Undavia and other buyers are struggling to receive their deposits for unfinished luxury condos in Boca Raton. The Mandarin Oriental Residences project has faced significant construction delays, impacting buyers' financial investments. A $417.7 million foreclosure lawsuit complicates the situation for prospective homeowners seeking refunds. Penn-Florida Companies attributes delays to various challenges, including rising construction costs and supply-chain issues.
title: Florida buyer's condo unfinished after $1.65m deposit; $418m foreclosure suit

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: More than 800 guests gathered at New York’s Waldorf Astoria on October 21, 2026, for an evening that combined celebrity appearances, philanthropy and a campaign against antisemitism and discrimination. The inaugural benefit gala of the Blue Square Alliance Against Hate, founded by New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, raised more than $32 million.
title: Patriots owner Robert Kraft's anti-hate gala raises over $32m in one night

author: ANUSHREE SINHA
description: Natalie Portman purchased a 550-square-metre mansion in Paris for €15.2 million in September 2023. Built in 1912, the four-storey property once served as an embassy before undergoing extensive renovation. Located near the Eiffel Tower, the residence features a garden, gym, library, wine cellar and a glass-roofed reception room. The actress bought the property months before her divorce from Benjamin Millepied was finalised.
title: Natalie Portman bought former Paris embassy near Eiffel Tower for $15.2m

author: KARAN MANRAL
title: ‘To hide roll manipulation’: Cong questions EC over withholding ECINET details

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: Indian and Australian army troops are actively participating in joint combat drills at the Foreign Training Node in Thiruvananthapuram, designated Exercise AUSTRAHIND 2026. This exercise, featuring approximately 240 servicemen including 120 from each country and a New Zealand observer team, is crafted to boost operational synergy with specialized activities such as combat swimming, ambush strategies, and focused aerial operations aimed at refining skills for joint coastal and island maneuvers.
title: India, Australia troops train for coastal, island warfare in AUSTRAHIND 2026

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A property transfer for just $1 has failed to shield a Kentucky couple’s land from a creditor seeking to recover an unpaid debt. In an October 23, 2026, opinion, the Kentucky Court of Appeals upheld an order allowing property assessed at approximately $210,000 to be sold to satisfy a judgment of $177,667.88, plus applicable costs and attorney fees.
title: Kentucky court allows sale of land transferred for $1 to cover $177,668 debt

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: The GST Appellate Tribunal ruled that airlines are eligible for GST refunds on cancelled flight tickets. Singapore Airlines was allowed to reclaim Rs 45.92 lakh after proving refunds were issued directly to passengers. The tribunal emphasized that airlines must provide ample documentation to establish the refund trail. This decision affects eight claims spanning from October 2019 to March 2021 amidst the Covid-19 pandemic.
title: Cancelled flight tickets: Airlines can claim GST refunds if fare and tax are returned

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Madison Square Garden Sports has admitted that an email offering New York Knicks employees free NBA championship rings was a phishing test. Staff who clicked were sent to a mandatory cybersecurity class, The Athletic reported. MSG called the ring lure an "unfortunate mistake," citing a recent hack that used stolen employee credentials, and says it will now gift more than 275 rings and jewellery worth over $3.7 million.
title: New York Knicks emailed staff free championship rings, those who clicked got a surprise

author: AASTHA JHA
title: 'Don't film missiles': India advises its nationals in Saudi Arabia amid ongoing Houthi strikes

author: PRATYUSH RAJ
description: Karnataka all-rounder is finding his feet in domestic cricket with batting, bowling and ability to deliver under pressure. From his father's love for Sachin Tendulkar and Rahul Dravid to the influence of Manish Pandey and coaches Yere Goud and Vinay Kumar, Manvanth reflects on his journey, ambitions, workload management and his love for anime.
title: 'This is Sachin, this is Dravid': How Manvanth Kumar fell in love with cricket

author: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI
description: Hindu organisations protested following an incident where eggs were allegedly thrown at a Durga Mata idol. The incident occurred during an immersion procession within Madanapet police station limits in Hyderabad. Police responded promptly after receiving a call and took the suspects into custody for investigation. A similar incident involving stone-pelting was reported during a Durga Visarjan procession in Maharashtra.
title: Tensions flare in Hyderabad after eggs 'thrown' at idol during procession

author: JYOTIRMOY HALDER
description: Ravichandran Ashwin feels Vaibhav Sooryavanshi struggled at No. 3 in India’s second T20I against New Zealand, scoring just four runs off eight balls. He believes Sanju Samson should bat at No. 3 if Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma and Samson play together. Ashwin also praised India’s middle order, highlighting the power and temperament of Tilak Varma, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Ramandeep Singh.
title: 'He was a fish out of water': Sooryavanshi's No. 3 role questioned after 2nd T20I

author: PRACHI KUMAWAT
description: The air quality in Delhi-NCR has substantially deteriorated, with the Air Quality Index registering an alarming 168, indicating unhealthy conditions. Toxic foam has resurfaced on the Yamuna River, particularly around Kalindi Kunj. In response, the Commission for Air Quality Management has initiated Stage 1 of the Graded Response Action Plan.
title: Toxic foam returns to Yamuna as AQI touches 168, GRAP-1 restrictions in force

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan are investing $50 million to establish STEM labs and an AI center at Sacramento State University. This generous donation aims to transform vacant state office buildings into a thriving downtown campus. California Governor Gavin Newsom emphasized this initiative will enhance the tech job talent pipeline, while the couple shifts their philanthropic efforts toward biomedical AI, aligning with Meta’s vision for innovation and education.
title: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan shift donations towards AI and science

author: VISHWA MOHAN
description: The decision taken this week by the UN body, the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD), in its emergency meeting assumes significance as it is not only a kind of admission that climate change causes such extreme events, but also an endorsement of the principle that historical polluters (developed nations) must contribute to the fund to assist vulnerable developing countries.
title: In first-ever climate crisis amends, Nepal to get $21.6 million

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion faces fresh delays as neighbors challenge his landscaping and fencing plans. Residents have raised concerns about wildlife safety, lake views and potential damage to an aging sewer line, with one neighbor citing $75,000 in repair costs. Kelce’s construction team says it has spent $7,500 on sewer repairs and adjusted the plans. However, local officials require further changes before the remaining landscaping work can proceed.
title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million mansion faces fresh setback as neighbors object

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ Kansas City Current have secured their third consecutive NWSL playoff berth after Portland’s 1-0 win over North Carolina. The club now aims to secure home-field advantage ahead of the postseason. Despite roster changes, Kansas City has maintained a record 31-game unbeaten home streak. Temwa Chawinga leads the team with 12 goals, while Croix Bethune has recorded 10 assists heading into the decisive final matches.
title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany's KC Current extend unbeaten home run to 31 games

author: ABHISHEK MISHRA
title: 'To kill people': Musk accuses Ukraine military of misusing Starlink for drone strikes

author: ABHISHEK MISHRA
title: 'Lie and fabrication': Iran denies Hormuz deal offer to US through Pakistan

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: India became the first team to play 300 men's T20 Internationals and also recorded their 200th win in the format. They reached the milestone in style, chasing down New Zealand's 180/5 with one ball to spare after losing five wickets for just 70 runs.
title: Team India's massive T20I record goes unnoticed; team miles ahead of Pakistan

author: PRABIN KALITA AND JOKEN ETE
description: Protests erupted in Pasighat, Arunachal Pradesh, against the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project on Friday night. After a 12-hour bandh ended peacefully, violent clashes began, injuring over 40 police personnel. The mob vandalized properties, set fire to government buildings, and damaged several police vehicles during the incident. Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu expressed concern and offered to hold talks with protesting groups.
title: Violent protests in Arunachal against Siang dam; MLAs’ homes looted, NHPC set ablaze

author: RAJ SHEKHAR JHA
description: Himanshu Bhau and Neeraj Faridpuria attempted to exploit immigration laws to gain asylum in the US. Their plan backfired when they were detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Both individuals used fake passports to evade law enforcement for several years. Indian and US authorities confirmed Bhau's identity through cross-verification of their backgrounds. Efforts are underway to expedite their deportation to India following their detention.
title: 'Fake passport to evade law': US asylum gamble blew gangster Bhau’s cover

author: TOI WORLD DESK
title: Illinois mansion owner gets just $25,000 for contents despite $8.75 million coverage

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Atlanta rapper and social media personality Shawty Dred, whose real name is Mercedes Reshard New, has been indicted in an alleged $4 million SNAP fraud scheme. Prosecutors claim he used stolen identities to create more than 350 fake accounts and EBT cards to siphon taxpayer-funded food benefits. He faces 63 counts, including mail fraud and aggravated identity theft.
title: Atlanta rapper Shawty Dred indicted in alleged $4M SNAP fraud case

author: TOI WORLD DESK
title: Minnesota man who'd never driven a bus stops rolling school bus with 19 kids

author: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI
description: India A will open their campaign against Nepal on November 20 before taking on Pakistan A two days later. They will play their final group-stage match against the UAE on November 24.
title: Drawn in same group, IND-PAK set to clash on Nov 22 in Rising Asia Cup

author: ABHISHEK MISHRA
title: ‘Saddam Hussein opened a cheesecake factory’: Obama’s jibe at Trump’s White House

author: RAJEEV SINGH
description: Speaking at an interactive dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on Minority Issues at the UN General Assembly's Third Committee, India's First Secretary at the Permanent Mission to the UN, Raghoo Puri, called out Pakistan's conduct and said its representatives should focus on the welfare of their own people instead of taking directions from the military.
title: ‘Prioritise welfare over military directives’: India raps Pak on minority rights

author: TOI
title: Couple die waiting for accident compensation in son’s death case

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Donald Trump’s niece Mary Trump has described his relationship with daughter Ivanka as “odd and off-putting” during an appearance on The Rest Is Politics podcast. She alleged that he showed little emotional interest in his children but developed an unusual attachment to Ivanka as she grew older. Mary also linked his parenting style to his own upbringing.
title: Mary Trump says Donald had 'no interest' in kids, had 'odd' fixation on Ivanka

author: ANUJA JAISWAL
description: Pressure from influential patients can lead to unnecessary medical procedures and a longer recovery time for others. Surgical oncologists at AIIMS Delhi emphasize that this practice undermines equal treatment for all patients. Prolonged hospital stays for VIPs can also negatively impact hospital resources and staff morale. The authors advocate for appropriate clinical protocols and transparent admission criteria to ensure fair patient care.
title: ‘VIP culture’ in hospitals can compromise patient safety, equitable care: AIIMS doctors

author: PRIYANGI AGARWAL
description: Real-time data from the new Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory highlights various pollution contributors. Vehicles were the largest contributor to Delhi's PM2.5 pollution at 25%. Secondary organic and inorganic aerosols also significantly contributed to pollution levels across the city. This facility, inaugurated by Union minister Jitendra Singh, aims to identify and assess pollution sources.
title: What’s Delhi breathing? IITM’s new lab decodes air mix
